$comment: Every change the edition makes to its base witness (text), and every difference of the other witness, classified (collation).

text.why: In the Saṃhitā the ṛk runs on into the next (पाँसुर इरावती, -e before i becoming -a); the sūktam recites it alone, so its last word stands in its pausal form, पाँसुरे (as in RV 1.22.17).

collation.note: W2 prints हि॒र्ण्यये॑न, dropping the a of hiraṇyayena; W1 and RV 1.35.2 have हिरण्ययेन.
The gaṇeśvara Brāhmaṇa writes the nasalised semivowel (दूतँव्वृणीमहे) for दूतं वृणीमहे.
The gaṇeśvara Brāhmaṇa (OCR) garbles होतारं as होता॑रखूँं; W1 and RV 1.12.1 have होतारम्.
W2 reads हि॒तेन॑व; W1 and RV 4.57.1 have हितेनेव (hitena iva, ‘as with a friend’).
W2 reads श्न्यप्त्रे; W1 has श्ञप्त्रे, the Taittirīya spelling of śnaptre (the two corners of the cart’s frame).
W2 writes the word-final -as of sthas before v unjoined (स्थस् विष्णोः), Weber’s practice; joined it is स्थो विष्णोः.
W1 writes श्ञ for श्न (पृश्ञिः), the Taittirīya spelling of the ś–n cluster.
